I bought a Uniden CMX760. I’m going to install it in my truck. (Toyota Tacoma so don’t get worked up.) I want to install it correctly. Tuning the antenna? Ok I will, but how?

Tuning the antenna is done with a SWR meter. The meter reads a ratio of transmitted "forward" power to reflected power. The objective is to reduce the reflected power as much as possible by ensuring the antenna has exactly the right length for the frequency. If the reflected power is worse on the lowest channel then your antenna is too short, if it's worse on the highest channel then the antenna is too long, a good tune will give the best results in the middle channels and gradually worsen towards the highest and lowest ones.

Just to throw you a slight curveball, the middle between ch1 and ch40 is NOT ch20 because there's 5 hidden channels in the lower half, 3a, 7a, 11a, 15a, and 19a historically allocated for radio controlled models, also the channels don't progress linearly around 23 it goes 21, 22, 24, 25, 23. Doesn't make much difference but worth keeping in mind to call 24 the middle not 20.

My last installation just came through the seal on the passenger door next to the hinge, and I decided to replace the cable every couple of years. Ended up only needing replacing once at about 5 years old. I had the cable through a hole in the brake light in a previous car, I've also done a radio install for someone else where the cable went through the hole for the rear screen washer in a truck that hadn't got that option installed.

There's usually a choice of ways to mount and cable if you look for them, but having a proper bolted through mounting as near as possible to the centre of the vehicle will always work best because the vehicle body is trying to work as part of the antenna system, it's your "ground plane" the same as the radials you see on some of the CB antennae on buildings or the lower element of a dipole. If your "ground plane" is only connected by the radio itself it's not going to work to its optimum efficiency and you may have difficulty tuning the antenna. If your antenna ends up off-centre then your transmission will be stronger in some directions than others, and if it's too far off centre (like it's right in one corner) then the antenna may refuse to "SWR" or tune at all. A badly tuned antenna will reflect power back into the radio where it is disposed of as heat, get the tuning far enough out and you could overheat and destroy the output transistor.
